pairs.evidence: src/app/api/harness/route.ts:351 POST /api/harness takes projectPath from an unauthenticated request body and makes it the cwd of a Claude session started with --dangerously-skip-permissions and Bash/Edit/Write (route.ts:343, executor.ts:239), so a key settable through the service door decides where a standing permission carve-out lets the agent write.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/harness/route.ts:351 The widened tier rule says a path key read by a skip-approval carve-out must come from the startup tier only. Here it comes from an HTTP body, and the route has no requireOperator. The sibling experiment/run route gets this right: it calls requireOperator(req) at line 19 and never takes the project path from the caller.

src/lib/harness-runs-db.ts:18 The route calls reapStrandedRuns() (route.ts:218). That function closes orphaned 'running' rows as a first-class 'interrupted' status, not as 'error', and an operator can reopen them.
src/app/api/harness/route.ts:138 Harness 'checkpoints' are git SHAs per area. They are not a stored conversation state that gets resumed, so the full-versus-delta mode question never comes up.

pairs.evidence: src/lib/blender-mcp/service.ts:23 This context is a serialized TCP wire client to the Blender addon, called from app code. I searched src/lib/blender-mcp for subagent, compaction, checkpoint, middleware and registerHook and found nothing: there is no hook chain, no extension loading, no model loop and no stored conversation state, which puts it on the mcp-tools side of the seam the golden path draws.
